hook.text: Tesla coined the term 'Gigafactory' because its Nevada plant produces batteries measured in gigawatt-hours.

buildup.text: A gigafactory is so large that the building itself must be designed to handle thermal expansion of its walls.

discovery.text: Mass production at this scale is the only way to drive battery costs low enough for affordable EVs.

twist.text: Europe, the US, and Asia are now in a gigafactory arms race, with over 200 plants planned globally.

climax.text: Each new factory cuts battery costs further, pushing EVs closer to price parity with gas cars.

punchline.text: Making batteries cheap requires building on a scale the world has never seen.

quiz.question: Why are gigafactories essential for the EV industry?
options: To produce batteries at scale and drive costs down

details.summary: Gigafactories are massive battery manufacturing plants that produce cells at enormous scale, driving down per-unit costs through automation, volume purchasing, and continuous process optimization.
details.whyItMatters: Battery cost is the largest barrier to affordable EVs. Gigafactories are essential for producing enough cells to supply millions of electric vehicles while achieving the economies of scale needed for low costs.
takeaways: Tesla coined the term for its Nevada lithium-ion cell plant
A single gigafactory can produce tens of gigawatt-hours annually
China, the US, and Europe are racing to build domestic capacity

faq.question: How many gigafactories are currently operating worldwide?
faq.answer: Dozens of gigafactories are operating or under construction across China, the US, and Europe. China leads with the most capacity, while the US and EU are rapidly expanding through incentive programs.

faq.question: Why are gigafactories so large?
faq.answer: Battery cell production involves many sequential steps including electrode coating, cell assembly, and formation cycling. Integrating all steps under one roof minimizes transport costs and quality losses.
